<header class="dg-head dg-head-chapter"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 3</p><h1 class="dg-title">Topological Manifolds</h1></header>
<div class="dg-motivation"><div class="dg-motivation-title">Motivation: Doing calculus without an ambient space</div><div class="dg-motivation-upper"><p>Spacetime should be a space on which we can do calculus without placing it inside a larger one. Calculus is defined on open subsets of <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d\)</span>, so the minimal requirement is that every point has a neighbourhood identified, through a chart <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X}\)</span>, with an open subset of <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d\)</span>. Saying that a neighbourhood is open, or that a chart is continuous, already needs a topology on the space itself. A single chart rarely suffices, since a compact space such as the sphere <span class="math inline">\(S^2\)</span> is not homeomorphic to any open subset of <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^2\)</span>. With several charts, a function <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> is differentiated through its chart representatives, which on an overlap are related by  <span class="math display">\[
        f \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1} = \big( f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big) \circ \big( \mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1} \big),
    \]</span>  so differentiability is independent of the chart only if the chart transition maps <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1}\)</span> are themselves differentiable.</p>
</div><div class="dg-motivation-lower">
<p><strong>Goal.</strong> Build, from a bare set, the space on which the rest of the notes is formulated.</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>Equip a set with a <strong>topology</strong>, which defines open sets, continuity and homeomorphisms, and with the Hausdorff and second countability conditions.</p></li>
<li><p>Define charts and atlases, and with them a <span class="math inline">\(d\)</span>-dimensional <strong>topological manifold</strong>, locally homeomorphic to <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>Require the chart transition maps to be <span class="math inline">\(C^\infty\)</span>, which defines a <strong>smooth manifold</strong>, together with smooth functions, curves and maps between manifolds.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>Spacetime will be a 4-dimensional smooth manifold, and coordinates will be nothing more than the values of its charts.</p></div></div>
<p>Figure <a class="dg-xref" href="../introduction/roadmaps.html#fig_roadmap_topology_to_fields" data-kind="figure" data-label="manifolds_roadmap">1.3</a> summarizes the construction, and Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="../examples/example-d-dim-mfld.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Example_d_dim_mfld">C.2</a> works out an explicit example of a <span class="math inline">\(d\)</span>-dimensional smooth manifold.</p>
